title: Introduction to R
text:
Statistical programming language
R is an interpreted programming language for statistical computing and graphics.

Created by statisticians Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman and first shared in 1993.
Considered a successor of the S language created by AT&T Bell Laboratories.
CRAN (The Comprehensive R Archive Network) was founded in 1997 by Kurt Hornik and Fritz Leisch.

CRAN hosts source code, executable files, documentation, and user-created packages.

title: Introduction to R
text:
Great research tool

Free: everyone can use it and contribute.
Advanced statistical methods that may not be available in other software.
Flexible for simple calculations or complex analysis reports.
Powerful graphics with reproducible figure generation.
Multiple output formats, including interactive outputs.
Reproducible research workflows that benefit the broader research community.

And many more.

title: Introduction to R

Install R
Installing R is straightforward.

Go to CRAN (Comprehensive R Archive Network).
Download R for Linux, Mac, or Windows. Latest version: R-4.6.1 (released on 2026-06-24, Happy Hop).
For Windows, install the base distribution.
For Mac, choose the installer matching your CPU architecture.



 All of the release names are references to Peanuts strips/films.

title: Introduction to R
text:
Some concepts

Packages: collections of functions, documentation, and data.
Functions: operations that return outputs, usually with arguments.
Assignment operator: <-
Case sensitivity: for example, great and Great are different.
Data modes: numeric, integer, character, complex, logical.
Data structures: vector, matrix, factor, list, data frame.

install.packages("pkgnames")
library(pkgnames)
mean(x)
sd(x)
class(x)
typeof(x)

title: Introduction to R
text:
Good practices in R

Start with a clean environment.
Prefer projects and avoid setwd() and rm(list = ls()) in scripts.
Set seeds for random processes with set.seed().
Follow a consistent coding style.
Comment code for clarity.
Use pipe operator |>.



“If the first line of your R script is rm(list = ls()), I will come into your office and SET YOUR COMPUTER ON FIRE.— Jenny Bryan”

title: Introduction to R
text:
Data preparation
This class assumes we are working with clean data that is ready for analysis.

Do not underestimate data preparation time.
Tidy data concept (Wickham, 2014):

Each variable forms a column.
Each observation forms a row.
Each type of observational unit forms a table.

tidyverse is very helpful for data preparation.

Reference: Wickham, H. (2014). Tidy Data. Journal of Statistical Software, 59(10), 1-23.

title: Introduction to R
text:
Initial data analysis (IDA)
IDA ensures transparency and integrity of preconditions for responsible statistical analyses.
It includes:

Metadata setup
Data cleaning
Data screening
Documentation and initial data reporting
Refining and updating the analysis plan

Data screening is related to descriptive statistics:

Distribution of single variables
Missing data
Association between variables

References:

Baillie et al. (2022), PLoS Computational Biology, 18(2): e1009819
Huebner et al. (2021), Observational Studies, 4: 171-192

Description
This repository has teaching materials for a hands-on Introduction to R as 2 days lessons. The workshop will introduce participants to the basics of R and RStudio. R is a simple programming environment that enables the effective handling of data, while providing excellent graphical support. RStudio is a tool that provides a user-friendly environment for working with R. These materials are intended to provide both basic R programming knowledge and its application for increasing efficiency for data analysis.
Note for participants: No prior experience with R is required for this workshop. We will walk through the hands-on exercises together. No need to preview the materials before the workshop.


Learning Objectives

R and R Studio: Familiarize with R and RStudio and navigate the RStudio.
R data types and structures: Understand the frequently-used data types and data structures in R.
Data manipulation essentials: Demonstrate the use of functions for wrangling data from various data structures.
Data visualization (Optional): Simple visualization using the ggplot2 package.
